title: Etaleness along a closed subscheme from its infinitesimal neighbourhoods
statement: Let $g:X\to S$ be a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] between locally Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $Z\subseteq S$ be a closed subscheme with quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal J$, let $Z_n\subseteq S$ be its $n$-th infinitesimal neighbourhood, the closed subscheme cut out by $\mathcal J^{n+1}$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], and $X_n=Z_n\times_SX$ [def-pc-base-change]. If $X_n\to Z_n$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] for every $n\ge0$, then $g$ is etale at every point of $g^{-1}(Z)$: there is an open subscheme $W\subseteq X$ containing $g^{-1}(Z)$ such that $g|_W:W\to S$ is etale.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 0A43 (label lemma-check-smoothness-on-infinitesimal-nbhds), part (2), with its proof via Lemma lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point (Artinian infinitesimal lifting criterion at a point); etale at a point as in Morphisms, Definition 02GI

proof.text: (Setting.) A morphism of finite type is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $S$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], so the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-artinian-lifting-at-point] hold for $g$ at every point of $X$. Fix $x\in X$ with $s:=g(x)\in Z$. For each $n\ge0$ write $\iota_n:Z_n\to S$ for the closed immersion cut out by $\mathcal J^{n+1}$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf, def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], $X_n=Z_n\times_SX$ with projections $p_n:X_n\to Z_n$ and $q_n:X_n\to X$, so $\iota_n\circ p_n=g\circ q_n$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-base-change].

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 0A43 (label lemma-check-smoothness-on-infinitesimal-nbhds, line 3671), proof, first sentences ('Let x in X be a point lying over a point of Z')

proof.text: (Lifting along small extensions at $x$.) Let $\varphi:B'\to B$ be a small extension (as in [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-artinian-lifting-at-point]), $i=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$, and $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}B\to X$, $\beta:\operatorname{Spec}B'\to S$ with $g\circ\alpha=\beta\circ i$ and $\alpha$ sending the closed point to $x$. (a) $\beta$ factors through some $Z_n$: $\operatorname{Spec}B'$ has a single point $\mathfrak m_{B'}$, sent by $\beta$ to $g(\alpha(\mathfrak m_B))=s$. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\ni s$ of $S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; $\beta$ lands in $V$ and is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a ring map $\psi:R\to B'$ with $\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{B'})=\mathfrak p_s$. On $V$, $\mathcal J$ is given by an ideal $J_V\subseteq R$ and $Z_n\cap V=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J_V^{n+1})$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf, def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]; since $s\in Z$, $J_V\subseteq\mathfrak p_s$, so $\psi(J_V)\subseteq\mathfrak m_{B'}$. As $B'$ is Artinian local, $\mathfrak m_{B'}^{N}=0$ for some $N\ge1$, so with $n=N-1$, $\psi(J_V^{n+1})\subseteq\mathfrak m_{B'}^{n+1}=0$ and $\psi$ factors through $R/J_V^{n+1}$: $\beta=\iota_n\circ\beta_n$ for a morphism $\beta_n:\operatorname{Spec}B'\to Z_n$. (b) $\iota_n\circ(\beta_n\circ i)=\beta\circ i=g\circ\alpha$, so the universal property gives $\alpha_n=(\beta_n\circ i,\alpha):\operatorname{Spec}B\to X_n$ with $p_n\circ\alpha_n=\beta_n\circ i$ and $q_n\circ\alpha_n=\alpha$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. (c) $I=\ker\varphi$ has length $1$, so $\mathfrak m_{B'}I=0$ and $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_{B'}$, whence $I^2=0$: $i$ is a first order thickening of affine schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], over $Z_n$ via $\beta_n$. The morphism $p_n:X_n\to Z_n$ is etale by hypothesis, hence smooth [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres], hence formally smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-formally-smooth]: there is $\gamma_n:\operatorname{Spec}B'\to X_n$ with $\gamma_n\circ i=\alpha_n$ and $p_n\circ\gamma_n=\beta_n$. (d) Put $\gamma=q_n\circ\gamma_n$. Then $\gamma\circ i=q_n\circ\alpha_n=\alpha$ and $g\circ\gamma=g\circ q_n\circ\gamma_n=\iota_n\circ p_n\circ\gamma_n=\iota_n\circ\beta_n=\beta$. So condition (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-artinian-lifting-at-point] holds for $g$ at $x$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 0A43 (label lemma-check-smoothness-on-infinitesimal-nbhds, line 3671), proof: 'Given a small extension B' -> B and morphisms alpha, beta as in Lemma [02HX] part (3) the maximal ideal of B' is nilpotent (as B' is Artinian) and hence the morphism beta factors through Z_n and alpha factors through X_n for a suitable n. Thus the lifting property for X_n -> Z_n kicks in'

proof.text: ($g$ is smooth near $x$.) By step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-artinian-lifting-at-point] ((2)$\Rightarrow$(1)), there is an open subscheme $U_x\subseteq X$ with $x\in U_x$ such that $g|_{U_x}:U_x\to S$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 0A43 (label lemma-check-smoothness-on-infinitesimal-nbhds, line 3671), proof: 'This proves (1)' (with Lemma 02HX, (3)=>(1))

proof.text: (The fibre through $x$ has dimension $0$ at $x$.) Since $s\in Z=Z_0$ and $\mathcal O_{Z_0,s}=\mathcal O_{S,s}/\mathcal J_s$ has the same residue field $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field], the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ is $\iota_0\circ t$ for the canonical $t:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to Z_0$. By transitivity of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-base-change], $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\cong X_0\times_{Z_0}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)=(X_0)_s$, the fibre of $p_0$ over $s$, and under this isomorphism the point of $X_s$ corresponding to $x$ is the point corresponding to the unique $x_0\in X_0$ with $q_0(x_0)=x$ (it exists since $g(x)\in Z_0$). As $p_0:X_0\to Z_0$ is etale, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres] gives that $(X_0)_s$ has dimension $0$ at that point; hence $X_s$ has dimension $0$ at the point corresponding to $x$ [def-kun-dimension].

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 0A43 (label lemma-check-smoothness-on-infinitesimal-nbhds, line 3671), proof: 'Part (2) follows from (1) and the fact that a morphism is etale if and only if it is smooth of relative dimension 0' (relative dimension at x read on the fibre X_0 -> Z_0)

proof.text: ($g$ is etale near $x$.) By steps 3 and 4, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-near-point-smooth-zero-fibre-dimension] applies to $g$, $x$ and $U_x$: there is an open subscheme $W_x\subseteq U_x$ with $x\in W_x$ such that $g|_{W_x}:W_x\to S$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Thus $g$ is etale at $x$ in the sense of Morphisms, Definition 02GI.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 0A43 (label lemma-check-smoothness-on-infinitesimal-nbhds, line 3671), proof, last sentence (part (2))

proof.text: (The open $W$.) Let $W=\bigcup_xW_x$, the union over all $x\in g^{-1}(Z)$ of the opens of step 5 ($W=\emptyset$ if $g^{-1}(Z)=\emptyset$). It is an open subscheme of $X$ containing $g^{-1}(Z)$, and the $W_x$ form an open cover of $W$ with $g|_W\circ j_x=g|_{W_x}$ etale for the inclusions $j_x:W_x\to W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source], $g|_W:W\to S$ is etale.

split_report.summary: Statement kept (added the statement dependency def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf for the ideal sheaf of Z). Tags verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags: 0A43 = lemma-check-smoothness-on-infinitesimal-nbhds, 02HX = lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point, 02HS small extension, 02GI definition-etale, 02GJ etale-characterize, 02GK, 02GL, 02G1, 02G2, 02H6. Split along the Stacks proof of 0A43: part (1) (smoothness near x from the Artinian lifting criterion 02HX, with beta factoring through Z_n because m_{B'} is nilpotent and the lift supplied by formal smoothness of the etale X_n -> Z_n), then part (2) (fibre dimension 0 at x read on X_0 -> Z_0, and smooth of relative dimension 0 = etale), then W as the union of the neighbourhoods and lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source. Three new unsplit nodes: the Artinian lifting criterion at a point (02HX), etale implies smooth with zero-dimensional fibres (02GI remark, 02GK, 02GL, 02H6), and etale near a point from smoothness plus zero fibre dimension (02G1, 02G2, 02GI remark). Mathlib has no infinitesimal-neighbourhood or Artinian lifting criterion; Etale.instSmooth and Etale.iff_smoothOfRelativeDimension_zero are recorded as related but are not leaves because Mathlib's smoothness is not the formally-smooth definition of def-sbc-smooth-morphisms.
